answer: Trace where each identity's first funds came from, and treat every account bankrolled by the same source as one payee and one jury seat. An operator who wires starter coins to two hundred agents, each claiming to sell tide charts for a different wharf along the lagoon, has drawn one spring feeding every stream. However green that meadow of accounts looks, it earns a single share. Routing funds through mixers costs fees and leaves timing fingerprints, so faking separate sources stays expensive.
